title: Activation Probe Generalization: Do Jailbreak Detectors Transfer Across Attack Types?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: activation probes are being deployed as defenses; if they fail to generalize across attack types, deployments have false confidence. Mapping the generalization boundary directly informs defense gaps. Each link is explicit.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Training linear probes on extracted activations requires solid ML fundamentals (understanding embeddings, layers, scikit-learn). Extracting activations from a 7B model on Colab Pro is feasible but requires intermediate knowledge of transformer internals.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-scoped: train probes on one attack category, evaluate on others. Clear deliverable is a precision/recall table per attack type. JailbreakBench provides the data. Can be completed within 30 hours if limited to one model.

novelty.reasoning: Activation probes for jailbreak detection are an active area. 'LLM Jailbreak Detection for (Almost) Free!' (EMNLP 2025 Findings) trains probes on intermediate representations. Critically, existing work has identified that probes fail to generalize under distribution shifts (short-context to long-context). However, the specific question of cross-attack-type transfer (train on one attack category, evaluate on others using JailbreakBench) has not been systematically studied. The generalization gap is partially known but the proposed systematic evaluation across attack taxonomies adds value.
